reasoning: Brief identifies as illustration — a character concept lineup for the game's four founder archetypes, hand-drawn, not photography. Style keyword mappings identical to the locked title-screen prompt: 'hand-drawn Xiaohei-style' maps to style.medium: illustration, style.rendering_technique: pencil rendered as wobbly felt-pen ink line with flat fills, texture.special: [uneven line weight, intentional overshoots]; 'colorful simple' maps to the locked RUNWAY! 7-color palette on paper cream #F2EAD3 with every hex pinned in technical_rules.strict_preserve. Subject type determination: four original IP creatures (fictional, Xiaohei-descended) — no real person block; each typed as character sharing one canonical body description (solid black bean body, white dot eyes, thin stick limbs, deadpan) with differentiation ONLY through props and one accessory each, which is itself the design rule being validated: if four identical bodies read as four distinct characters through props alone, the entire 360-image character workload collapses. Prop assignments derived from the PRD archetypes: The Hacker = laptop + energy drink cans, The Hustler = necktie + two phones, The Dropout = backwards cap + skateboard, The Ex-FAANG PM = lanyard badge + coffee cup with sticky notes. Each creature performs a small characteristic action rather than posing — Xiaohei law: the creature acts, never decorates. exact_text: the four archetype names, mapped verbatim into text_rendering.elements as hand-lettered labels under each character. Composition: single row of four on flat cream, generous whitespace, no panel borders — this is a character sheet the artist and future prompts will reference. Ambiguities resolved: 16:9 to match the game's native ratio and allow side-by-side comparison; names lettered in ink black with one coral accent underline each rather than colored text, to keep the sheet quiet. Operation: text_to_image. No reference images. negative_prompt covers the style's failure modes: cuteness, gradients, vector cleanliness, 3D, anime, panel frames. CHARACTER v2 LOCK applied (matches concept_01): single cowlick spike, permanent forward lean, mismatched white oval eyes, tiny cream sneakers with one untied lace — with two archetype-level expressive exceptions written into the descriptions: the Dropout's lean reads as slouch, and the Ex-FAANG PM stands straight with both laces tied (discipline as the joke).

character.source: The Hacker — founder archetype from the game RUNWAY!, original IP descended from the Xiaohei illustration IP
character.description: Identical base creature: solid ink-black wobbly bean body leaning slightly forward (perpetually mid-hustle, even standing still), a single ink cowlick spike on the head, two blank white oval eyes subtly mismatched (left a touch bigger), no mouth, thin stick limbs, tiny paper-cream sneakers with ink outlines (one lace untied), completely deadpan. Sits cross-legged (still somehow leaning forward), typing on a muted blue laptop with tiny code squiggles on the screen, cowlick bent from being slept on. A pyramid of three sunny yellow energy drink cans at its side. No hoodie, no clothing beyond the sneakers — the laptop and cans carry the whole identity.
character.consistency_rule: identical base body to all other RUNWAY! characters — solid black forward-leaning bean, single cowlick spike, mismatched white oval eyes, tiny cream sneakers, deadpan; only props, one accessory, and pose differ

usage_context.purpose: validate the core character-design bet: four identical deadpan black creatures made distinct by props alone; if this reads, the entire character asset workload collapses to prop variations
usage_context.usage_notes: Inferences made: 16:9 chosen for side-by-side comparison at the game's native ratio. Prop kits derived from the PRD archetype table — Hacker (build-focused: laptop, energy drinks), Hustler (sell-focused: tie, two phones), Dropout (speed-focused: cap, skateboard, abandoned diploma), Ex-FAANG PM (process-focused: lanyard, coffee, sticky-note grid). Each character performs its identity as an action rather than posing, per the Xiaohei rule that the creature must do the work, not decorate. The archetype names are lettered in ink with coral underlines rather than colored text to keep the sheet quiet and let silhouettes dominate.
